answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce token in a public, slashable bond before it may place orders or earn reputation. A plume of new accounts then costs the attacker one bond per account, tying up capital; if an account is caught double-spending or breaking agreed rules, its bond is forfeited. Splitting one stake across aliases does not multiply the value at risk, so the attacker must provide genuinely more capital to gain more influence. A wharf can host the exchange, while a sparrow-sized account faces the same bond rule.
